test_title: PYST 12: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I - GA (Held On: 10 Jun, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: In the 2024 Supreme Court case 'Aligarh Muslim University vs Naresh Agarwal (November 2024)', what did the majority of the Court hold regarding the minority status of educational institutions?

options.text: An institution must be entirely managed by the minority community to qualify as a minority institution.
Institutions created before 1950 can still be considered minority institutions, even if incorporated by statute.
Educational institutions established by statute cannot be considered minority institutions under Article 30(1).
The majority of the judges (4 out of 7 in opinion) of the bench concluded the Azeez Basha case and violated the AMU's minority status.

solution:
The correct answer is __**Institutions created before 1950 can still be considered minority institutions, even if incorporated by statute**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The majority opinion in the Supreme Court case 'Aligarh Muslim University vs Naresh Agarwal (November 2024)' upheld that institutions established before 1950 can retain minority status under Article 30(1).
 
• This decision revisited key aspects of the landmark Azeez Basha case (1968), which had previously ruled against AMU's minority status.
 
• The judgment clarified that incorporation by statute does not automatically strip minority communities of their rights under Article 30(1).
 
• The Court emphasized historical and constitutional contexts, recognizing the unique circumstances under which institutions like AMU were established.
 
• This ruling reinforces the protection granted to minority educational institutions under the Indian Constitution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 30(1) of the Indian Constitution:**

 
 
• Grants minority communities the right to establish and administer educational institutions of their choice.
 
• Ensures protection of cultural and linguistic rights for minorities.
 
• Is intended to preserve the diversity and pluralism of India's education system.
 
 
 
• **Azeez Basha Case (1968):**
 
 
• The Supreme Court ruled that AMU was not a minority institution because it was established by an Act of Parliament, not by the Muslim community.
 
• This judgment had significant implications for minority rights in India.
 
 
 
• **Aligarh Muslim University (AMU):**
 
 
• Founded in 1920, AMU is one of India's premier educational institutions with historical importance for the Muslim community.
 
• It was established by Sir Syed Ahmed Khan as the Mohammedan Anglo-Oriental College, which later became AMU.
 
 
 
• **Minority Educational Institution:**
 
 
• An institution established by a minority community to preserve its culture, language, or religion.
 
• Such institutions are protected under Article 30(1) of the Indian Constitution.
